title: How Much Fiber in Spinach? 4.3g per Cup
description: Spinach: about 4.3 g of fiber per 1 cup, cooked (15% DV), from USDA FoodData Central. Portion table, comparisons, free calculator.
h1: How much fiber is in spinach?

answer.note: USDA FoodData Central, Spinach, cooked, boiled, drained, without salt

intro: Spinach ranks #5 of 10 vegetables on this site for fiber per serving. Every figure below is scaled from USDA FoodData Central, the same data the calculator uses.

dataTable.caption: Fiber in spinach by portion
dataTable.note: Fiber and calories are scaled from USDA FoodData Central per-100 g values (rows listed under Sources). % Daily Value uses the 28 g reference on U.S. Nutrition Facts labels. Brands, ripeness, and cooking change real values.

sections.heading: How much fiber is in spinach?
paragraphs: USDA FoodData Central lists spinach, cooked, boiled, drained, without salt at 2.4 g of fiber per 100 g. One serving (1 cup, cooked; 180 g) therefore has about 4.3 g of fiber and 41 calories. That is 15% of the 28 g Daily Value on U.S. Nutrition Facts labels, or 17% of a 25 g day and 11% of a 38 g day.
Spinach shows how much cooking changes a portion. A cup of raw leaves weighs only 30 g, while a cup of cooked spinach is about six times that, so the cooked cup has many times the fiber.

sections.heading: Raw salad vs cooked spinach
paragraphs: A big raw spinach salad looks like a lot of food but adds only a gram or two of fiber. Wilting the same spinach into a pasta or curry concentrates it.
Frozen chopped spinach is already cooked down, so a cup of thawed frozen spinach is closer to the cooked row.

sections.heading: How spinach compares with other vegetables
paragraphs: Of the 10 vegetables on this site, spinach ranks #5 for fiber per typical serving and #3 for fiber per calorie. That works out to 10.4 g of fiber per 100 calories, a high ratio: you get a lot of fiber for the calories.

Close neighbors by serving: [Brussels sprouts](/fiber-in-brussels-sprouts) at 4.1 g (1 cup, cooked); [green beans](/fiber-in-green-beans) at 4 g (1 cup, cooked); [kale](/fiber-in-kale) at 4.7 g (1 cup, cooked). Across all 50 foods in the [fiber-in-foods table](/fiber-in-foods), spinach is #6 for fiber per calorie.

sections.heading: Adding spinach to your day
paragraphs: Wilt a few handfuls of spinach into eggs, soups, lentils, or pasta sauce. A cup of cooked spinach adds about 4 g.

Example: 1 cup cooked spinach, 1 cup lentils, 1/2 cup brown rice. Using the same USDA values as the calculator, that comes to about 21.5 g of fiber, with 4.3 g from the spinach. Adjust the amounts in the calculator to match your plate.

faqs.q: How much fiber is in 100 g of spinach?
faqs.a: 2.4 g, according to USDA FoodData Central (Spinach, cooked, boiled, drained, without salt). That is the figure every portion on this page is scaled from.

faqs.q: How much fiber is in spinach (1 cup, raw)?
faqs.a: About 0.7 g (Spinach, raw), for 30 g. Weigh your portion or edit grams in the calculator for a closer estimate.
Cooked, it is a good source. Raw, a single cup is small. It depends on whether you count raw volume or cooked.
Cooked, they are close. Cooked spinach is about 4.3 g (1 cup, cooked) and cooked kale about 4.7 g per cup.
